Sergio —

Quick summary from infra after 20m of triage:
- Cause: Dedicated GPU pool for ClearCore (pool-cc-03) is showing sustained GPU utilization > 96% on two nodes and intermittent OOM-driven task evictions. That explains the queuing and 5xxs.
- Throughput accounting still shows requests accepted at the reserved QPS, but the runtime is failing to keep up with peak burstiness due to smaller-than-expected KV cache hit and long tail sequences in production prompts.

Immediate mitigation (can be enacted in ~18–30 mins):
1) Temporarily attach two warm standby GPUs to pool-cc-03 (hot-swap) — ETA 18m, risk: minor transient reconnects for inflight requests.
2) Apply a soft rate-shed for background/low-priority routes from ClearCore (we can implement token-based tagging) — ETA 12m, requires their approval for temporary degradation on non-critical flows.
3) Enable aggressive KV prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes used in merchant lookups (runtime config flip) — ETA 6m, low risk.

Longer term: increase dedicated pool headroom by 25% for this reservation or move ClearCore to a slightly larger instance type; I'll attach the proposed scaling-playbook.md with cost delta.

I'll start step 3 immediately and queue step 1. Please confirm if we should proceed with step 2 (Marissa to coordinate with Claire).

Vivek Kulkarni
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

  • Attaching temporary warm GPUs to the pool (~18–30m) to restore headroom;
  • Optionally rate-shedding non-critical background flows if you approve — this would be scoped to batch jobs only.
- ETA for visible improvement: ~10–25 minutes for latency to return to normal; full stabilization as GPUs come online ~30 minutes.
